questions.question_text:
A circle has a radius of $8\text{ cm}$.
What is the exact length of an arc subtending a central angle of $\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\text{ radians}$?

options.why: Multiplied by diameter instead of radius ($2r\theta$).
Divided angle by radius instead of multiplying ($l = \theta / r$).
Omitted $\pi$ from the calculated arc length.

questions.question_text:
A circle has a radius of $10\text{ cm}$.
Find the exact arc length subtended by a central angle of $45^{\circ}$.

options.why: Substituted the angle in degrees directly into $l=r\theta$ without converting to radians.
Used an angle conversion corresponding to $90^{\circ}$ instead of $45^{\circ}$.
Divided degrees by $180$ but omitted $\pi$ from the radian value.

questions.question_text:
An arc of length $14\pi\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\text{ radians}$ at the centre of a circle.
What is the radius of the circle?

options.why: Multiplied arc length by angle instead of dividing ($r = l\theta$).
Divided angle by arc length instead of arc length by angle.
Retained $\pi$ in the linear radius measurement.

questions.question_text:
An arc of length $15\text{ cm}$ in a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle $\theta$ at the centre.
What is $\theta$ in radians?

options.why: Divided radius by arc length instead of arc length by radius.
Multiplied radius by arc length instead of dividing.
Appended $\pi$ to a dimensionless decimal angle quotient.

questions.question_text:
A minor arc in a circle of radius $4\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$.
What is the exact length of the major arc?

options.why: Calculated the minor arc length instead of the major arc length.
Subtracted from $\pi$ instead of $2\pi$ when finding the major central angle.
Calculated the entire circle circumference.

questions.question_text:
A pendulum of length $60\text{ cm}$ swings through an arc of $18\text{ cm}$.
What is the angle of swing in radians?

options.why: Formed the ratio $18 \div 60$ correctly but labelled the result in degrees; $l = r\theta$ only holds when $\theta$ is in radians.
Inverted the formula and divided the radius by the arc length, $60 \div 18 = 3.33$, instead of arc length by radius.
Made both slips at once: divided radius by arc length to get $60 \div 18 = 3.33$, then labelled that answer in degrees rather than radians.

questions.question_text:
A circle has a radius of $18\text{ cm}$.
Find the exact arc length subtended by an angle of $150^{\circ}$ at the centre.

options.why: Substituted degrees directly into $l=r\theta$ without converting to radians.
Divided by $360$ instead of $180$ during degree-to-radian conversion.
Used the diameter instead of the radius.

questions.question_text:
An arc of length $l = 6\pi\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle $\theta$ in a circle of radius $r$.
If $\theta \leq \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$, what is the smallest possible value of $r$?

options.why: Multiplied the arc length by the angle boundary.
Multiplied $6$ by $\frac{3}{4}$ instead of dividing.
Inverted the quotient when solving the inequality for radius.

questions.question_text:
A car wheel of diameter $60\text{ cm}$ rolls without slipping through an angle of $25\text{ radians}$.
How far does the car travel in metres?

options.why: Used diameter instead of radius ($60 \times 25$).
Did not convert centimetres to metres ($750\text{ cm} \to 750\text{ m}$).
Divided the radius by the angle ($60 \div 25$).
